terms.comment: Our use, for a transfer or a transit on a journey: classically a going over, a passage (Lewis & Short). The reference works have only the verb, Traupman’s trānscendere in + acc., to transfer to another train (pp. 219, 397).

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 219, 397.
